questions.question: If a drunk passenger is on your bus, what should you do?

options.text: Force them to get off the bus right away.
Wait until you reach a safe area, like a stop or well-lit place, before asking them to exit.
Give them coffee to help them sober up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you reach a safe area, like a stop or well-lit place, before asking them to exit.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for the drunk passenger's safety. Let them exit at a safe location, such as the next scheduled stop or a well-lit area where other people are present.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you use the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down quickly.
Press it down slowly and smoothly.
Lift it up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal down in a smooth, gradual way.

questions.question: What is important when driving?

options.text: Plan ahead for dangerous situations.
Enjoy the scenery.
Turn your head around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead for dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: While driving, constantly watch for hazards on the road. Think ahead about what you will do if those hazards become emergencies.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of these is NOT a concern?

options.text: Air pressure that is too high
Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch in the grooves
Mixing radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch in the grooves
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is not too low or too high. Make sure front tires have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove. Never mix radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with strong regard for other drivers' safety.
Driving in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for the safety of other drivers.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to turn, what should you do?

options.text: Skip the turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of tire failure?

options.text: A loud sound
Vibration
Smoother steering

questions.correctAnswerText: Smoother steering
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang sound or heavy thumping and vibration. Heavy steering or the rear of the vehicle fishtailing are also signs. Smoother steering is not a sign of tire failure.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: No, they are not safe.
Yes, only on the rear tires.
Yes, only when carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not safe.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs should never be used.

questions.question: Is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, if you are contacting your employer.
Yes, when driving on rural roads.
No, it is never allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is never allowed.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and never permitted while operating a vehicle.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of traffic around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Can hear traffic sounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle approaching and may do dangerous things because they do not know you are there.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?

options.text: Speeding
Stopping
Under-inflated tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding
questions.explanation: Drivers going too fast cause most injuries and deaths in work zones. Always slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a retarder and the drive wheels have poor traction, what happens?

options.text: The wheels will be more likely to skid
The wheels will have better traction
The wheels will lock up

questions.correctAnswerText: The wheels will be more likely to skid
questions.explanation: A retarder can cause the drive wheels to skid when they have poor traction. Turn off the retarder when driving on wet, icy, or snowy roads.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer
There may be extra weight in the front of the vehicle
Cargo may fall out of the trailer
Trailers are not made to be driven in reverse

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only back up if it is absolutely necessary.

questions.question: What emergency equipment should a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment are:

options.text: Only needed in vehicles transporting hazardous materials
Only needed for interstate travel
Required in all commercial motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Required in all commercial motor vehicles
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: When should you signal before turning?

options.text: Before you start the turn
Just before you turn, then turn off the signal
Only if other vehicles are in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the turn
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off after the turn is complete.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, how should you hold them?

options.text: Between your body and oncoming traffic
Behind your back so other drivers do not see them until they are placed
As low as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Between your body and oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic when placing them on the road.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Do not drive in fog if you can avoid it
Use your high beam headlights
Turn off your lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive in fog if you can avoid it
questions.explanation: Fog is very dangerous and should be avoided when possible. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: Which vehicles are most affected by strong winds?

options.text: Light vehicles
Heavy vehicles
Vehicles with open windows

questions.correctAnswerText: Light vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control a vehicle. Light commercial vehicles are especially affected by strong winds.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles driving behind a truck?

options.text: They may not see objects in front of the truck
They have a clear view of the road ahead
They do not need to signal

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not see objects in front of the truck
questions.explanation: Your truck blocks the view of drivers behind you. They cannot see hazards ahead. Flash your brake lights and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.
